In [[functional analysis]] and related areas of [[mathematics]] a '''FK-space''' or '''Fréchet coordinate space''' is a [[sequence space]] equipped with a [[topological structure]] such that it becomes a [[Fréchet space]].<ref name="r004">{{cite book | title=North-Holland Mathematics Studies | chapter=Chapter 4 FK Spaces | publisher=Elsevier | year=1984 | issn=0304-0208 | doi=10.1016/s0304-0208(08)72555-6 | page=51–73}}</ref> FK-spaces with a [[normable topology]] are called [[BK-spaces]].

There only exists one topology to turn a sequence space into a [[Fréchet space]], namely the [[topology of pointwise convergence]]. Thus the name ''coordinate space'' because a sequence in an FK-space converges if and only if it converges for each coordinate.

FK-spaces are examples of [[topological vector spaces]]. They are important in [[summability theory]].

==Definition==

A '''FK-space''' is a [[sequence space]] of <math>X</math>, that is a [[linear subspace]] of vector space of all complex valued sequences, equipped with the topology of [[pointwise convergence]].

We write the elements of <math>X</math> as
<math display=block>\left(x_n\right)_{n \in \N}</math> with <math>x_n \in \Complex</math>.

Then sequence <math>\left(a_n\right)_{n \in \N}^{(k)}</math> in <math>X</math> converges to some point <math>\left(x_n\right)_{n \in \N}</math> if it converges pointwise for each <math>n.</math> That is
<math display=block>\lim_{k \to \infty} \left(a_n\right)_{n \in \N}^{(k)} = \left(x_n\right)_{n \in \N}</math>
if for all <math>n \in \N,</math>
<math display=block>\lim_{k \to \infty} a_n^{(k)} = x_n</math>

==Examples==

The sequence space <math>\omega</math> of all [[Space of complex valued sequences|complex valued sequences]] is trivially an FK-space.

==Properties==

Given an FK-space of <math>X</math> and <math>\omega</math> with the topology of pointwise convergence the [[inclusion map]]
<math display=block>\iota : X \to \omega</math>
is a [[Continuous function (topology)|continuous function]].

==FK-space constructions==

Given a countable family of FK-spaces <math>\left(X_n, P_n\right)</math> with <math>P_n</math> a countable family of [[seminorm]]s, we define
<math display=block>X := \bigcap_{n=1}^{\infty} X_n</math>
and
<math display=block>P := \left\{p_{\vert X} : p \in P_n\right\}.</math>
Then <math>(X,P)</math> is again an FK-space.
